change: A synthetic content pack generated by Swift code in the engine's tests (engine/Tests/NTSDEngineTests/Synthetic/): every byte authored in code, written to a temporary folder (TMPDIR) and removed; a synthetic profile (EngineTestRules with invented interface names) and a content identity computed from the generated manifests. Tests load every package through the engine's public loaders. tools/scan_original_bytes.py gains --engine-files (a folder's raw bytes, generated DATs also decrypted) and classes for a generated pack's format structure. No engine source change.
implementation: one owner agent wrote the generator and tests (no engine source change needed); the loop then adopted the review's changes

portraits of an invented size (37x41 instead of 40x45)
a pinned digest of the pack and the catalog checksum for cross-host comparison
the read-back tests labelled as generator invariants
comments on the frame-number conventions and the music rate
review.correction: the review said shadowsize does not follow from the shadow image and no engine rule needs it; removing it broke the background parse (the loader reads the token after the shadow path as a label and the next two numbers into the record at 0x14/0x18, OriginalBackgroundLoader.swift:67-74): it stays, now half the generated 30x9 shadow (15 4), asserted by the catalog test

process: the owner agent's first two runs wrote about 0.77 MB of temporary packs under /var/folders on the internal disk (FileManager.temporaryDirectory ignores TMPDIR on Darwin); the tests removed them; the generator now uses TMPDIR and every run here set it to NTSD-Builds
a DAT ending in one newline gave a different checksum with VC80's read-ahead; every generated DAT ends in two whitespace characters
limits: loading only: no session path (the catalog test calls loadWithFiles with its own backing, not OriginalApplicationCatalogSession), no headless start, no match (E7d)
the record all zero with an all-ones mask: the engine's undefined-storage checks never fire on it
the catalog's music entries are text placeholders; sprite pixels are not checked; the music playback test is Darwin-only
the synthetic rules inherit EngineTestRules' NTSD-derived rows (weaponBreak [100: 5], frames10, 217/218)
the scans find copies of 15 bytes or more under the classes' caps
